description: I am an astronautical engineer who specifies in propulsion working with a data analyst, feel welcomed to reach out if you're passionate about combustion science or web development, we prioritize having fun in the process!
summary: Fire is one of the biggest risks in space, and crews cannot evacuate or call firefighters. Microgravity changes how fire behaves, while NASA's fire-safety research is scattered across many experiments and hard to compare. Flame Atlas brings that research into one place. At its core, a Super Intelligence AI agent turns complex questions into clear, sourced answers. Users can compare experiments, find which results matter most for the ISS, a lunar base, a Mars base or a rover, and see where evidence is missing, partial or still planned. Flame Atlas gives engineers and astronauts one clear, trustworthy view of fire-safety evidence for safer space missions.
details:
What it does

Flame Atlas is a fire-safety research platform for space missions. It brings NASA microgravity combustion research into one place and adds an AI assistant. Users explore 15 curated investigations, compare oxygen limits, fuels and test conditions, and see which studies matter most for the ISS, a lunar base, a Mars base or a pressurised rover. They can ask questions in plain language and get sourced answers. A separate search covers 133 NASA PSI investigation records, including ones outside the curated set.

Benefits and impact

- Cuts the time needed to find and compare fire-safety evidence.

- Avoids invented answers by grounding every number in data.

- Makes gaps visible, so engineers know what is unknown.

- Supports safer design of spacecraft, lunar and Mars habitats, and rovers.

- Helps researchers and non-specialists ask complex questions without learning each dataset.

Data

- Source: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI), including experiment metadata and cleaned tables, including DATA files and documents .

- 18 cleaned experiment tables and 15 curated investigations.

- An offline pipeline downloads metadata at one request per second, validates archives, records checksums and source links, and caches responses. The app never scrapes NASA at request time.

- One canonical dataset feeds both the dashboard and the API. Reference metadata is the single source of truth.

- Automated tests and build checks compare the JavaScript and Python outputs, so the two pipelines cannot drift.

- Units are normalised. Missing, partial, planned-only and assumed data are labelled.

How it works

- React + three.js dashboard: mission environments, rankings, charts, experiment detail panel, CSV/JSON export.

- FastAPI backend: read-only public API.

- Super Intelligence AI agent: answers through 13 deterministic tools for schema, search, comparison, queries, scoring, gaps, row data, exports and catalogue search.

- Every number and citation must come from a tool result. Ungrounded answers and citations are rejected.

- Optional ONNX reranker improves catalogue search ranking; BM25 remains the default.

- Scope controls limit the agent to selected PSI records; environment and oxygen probe produce independent rankings.

- Tested with Node's test runner and pytest; traced with Logfire and Jaeger.

Tools used

- Languages: JavaScript/JSX, Python, HTML/CSS.

- Frontend: React, Vite, three.js.

- Backend: FastAPI, Pydantic AI, pandas, Uvicorn, Gemini model.

- Search/ML: BM25, ONNX Runtime, tokenizers.

- Data: Node.js, Python, JSON, CSV.

- Operations: npm, uv, Docker, Docker Compose, OCI Run container.

- Claude and hosting: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure , Google Cloud

Creativity and considerations

- Creative mix: immersive dashboard plus conversational, evidence-grounded analysis.

- Environment-specific ranking, not one generic list.

- "Honest data" design: planned tests are never shown as measured results.

- Full-catalogue search finds leads; curated data remains the citable evidence.

- The team considered data quality, unit differences, provenance, safety, rate limits, reproducibility, deployment simplicity, accessibility and reduced motion.
